ctx.x: Great with life itself, and with our heritage. In this series of heritage programs, we are privileged to meet Mr. Louis Armstrong, the internationally known New Orleans jazz trumpeter and band leader. In this fourth program, Mr. Armstrong and his guests, Mr. Benny Benack, jazz trumpeter, band leader, and assistant director of the University of Pittsburgh Band, and Dr. Frederick Dorian, musicologist at Carnegie Institute of Technology and program annotator for the Pittsburgh Symphony, will discuss jazz is just…

A lot of people start breaking music down, and they say, this is good music, and that's bad, whether it's symphony or jazz. And actually, I think music is music, and I think there's a purpose for music. Maybe that's the thing. Maybe we shouldn't say it's good technically, or it's good this way, or structurally. Maybe there's a feeling we should get out of music. What do you think about it? You say, a lot of people that go in and do all that, they don't know anything about music. You understand? items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-16
items.q: Robert McCulley, Mr. Adam Lynch, and Mr. Benny Benet. In part four of this series, Mr. Armstrong and his guests will discuss Jazz is Just Good Music.

ctx.x: Well, uh, you know, here's something else. They, uh, I've heard, or you've heard, that American jazz is really dug over in Europe and, uh, all over the world, and it's a tremendous influence. They say that, uh, sometimes our jazz music is, uh, better than, uh, some of our diplomats. It does more good, uh.

Yeah, well, I don't talk about singing like that, because some people, uh, I think they can't look too far. I don't know, they probably don't go here as diplomats or something. You know what I mean, but, but the music from, uh, the people I run into, they go there with all good, happiness, pain, and that, that's the way that curtain rides. You know what I mean? Your boys will play with you. They feel the same way as you do. Yeah, they, uh, always tell them don't mess up their hustle. Mm-hmm. That means so much.…
